step: Visa Pathway Assessment — 482 TSS vs 186 ENS vs Other
deadline_label: Before issuing a job offer to a non-citizen — at least 16 weeks ahead for 482 TSS; 26+ weeks for 186 ENS
non_obvious_official_guidance: Australia's primary employer-sponsored visa pathways are Subclass 482 (Temporary Skill Shortage — TSS), Subclass 186 (Employer Nomination Scheme — ENS, permanent residence), and Subclass 494 (Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional — Provisional). The 482 has two streams: Short-term (up to 2 years) and Medium-term (up to 4 years). The 186 ENS has two streams: Direct Entry and Temporary Residence Transition (TRT, for existing 482 holders of 3+ years).
non_obvious_actual_reality: Three critical traps: (1) The available visa stream depends entirely on the ANZSCO occupation code — occupations on the Short-term Skilled Occupation List (STSOL) access only the Short-term 482 stream (max 2 years, no permanent residence pathway from within Australia in most cases); occupations on the Medium and Long-term Strategic Skills List (MLTSSL) access the Medium-term stream (4 years, PR pathway via 186 TRT after 3 years). HR teams routinely assume all 482 holders are on the same path. (2) The process involves three separate Department of Home Affairs (DHA) applications — Standard Business Sponsorship, Nomination, and the individual Visa — each with its own fee and processing queue. Total employer cost per sponsored employee ranges AUD 7,000–15,000+ depending on stream and applicant profile. Nominations and visas can be lodged concurrently, but SBS must be approved first — an unapproved sponsor cannot lodge a valid nomination. (3) New Zealand citizens hold a Subclass 444 (Special Category Visa) granted automatically on arrival and can work freely without employer sponsorship — attempting to sponsor an NZ citizen on a 482 is both unnecessary and a waste of fees.
non_obvious_action_required: Before drafting any job offer to a non-citizen: look up the ANZSCO code for the role at homeaffairs.gov.au and confirm which occupation list applies. If the occupation is on neither list, 482 is unavailable and alternative pathways must be assessed. Confirm whether the entity holds current Standard Business Sponsorship. Brief the candidate explicitly on whether the role leads to a permanent residence pathway before they accept the offer.

step: Standard Business Sponsorship (SBS) Application
deadline_label: Before nomination can be lodged — allow 4–8 weeks for DHA processing
non_obvious_official_guidance: An employer must be an approved Standard Business Sponsor before lodging a 482 nomination. SBS approval lasts 5 years. The application requires evidence of lawful business operation in Australia, a genuine need for the role, and commitment to Australian workplace law compliance.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Two non-obvious traps: (1) SBS approval does not automatically transfer through corporate restructures, mergers, entity conversions, or ABN changes. A newly created entity — including a subsidiary formed post-acquisition — must apply for SBS from scratch even if the underlying business is identical. This has stranded sponsored employees mid-transfer when HR assumed the acquired entity's SBS carried over. (2) Approved sponsors carry ongoing compliance obligations that DHA audits: training benchmarks (1.5% of payroll for businesses with annual payroll ≥ AUD 10M; AUD 1,200 per sponsored worker per year for smaller businesses), record-keeping for 4 years, and notification of prescribed events within 28 days (e.g., change of legal name, business address, or when a sponsored worker ceases employment). Sponsors who fail audits can have SBS cancelled — which immediately affects all 482 visa holders they currently sponsor.
non_obvious_action_required: Before any hiring process, check the entity's SBS status in ImmiAccount. If a corporate restructure is planned, seek immigration advice before the restructure completes — sometimes a pre-approved novation of sponsorship can be arranged, but it requires DHA's agreement. Brief finance on training benchmark obligations as a recurring annual compliance cost, not a one-off.

step: Nomination Lodgement — 482 TSS or 186 ENS (including Labour Market Testing)
deadline_label: After SBS approval — concurrent lodgement with the visa application is permissible; allow 6–12 weeks processing
non_obvious_official_guidance: The employer nominates a specific position for a specific worker. The nominated occupation must correspond to an approved ANZSCO code and occupation list. The employer must demonstrate: the position is genuine, the salary meets or exceeds the Temporary Skilled Migration Income Threshold (TSMIT), and Labour Market Testing (LMT) was conducted within the required timeframe.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Labour Market Testing is consistently the largest source of nomination rejections. Requirements: the employer must have advertised the position in Australia for at least 4 weeks, using at least 2 methods (e.g., Seek.com.au plus LinkedIn, or employer website plus an industry publication), within the 4 months immediately before lodging the nomination. DHA officers apply significant scrutiny to ad quality — extremely brief ads, ads with unrealistically narrow requirements, or ads that were clearly never intended to attract local applicants are rejected. The TSMIT as of 1 July 2023 is AUD 70,000 — guaranteed annual earnings (base salary plus super) must exceed this threshold; if the market salary for the occupation exceeds TSMIT, the nominated salary must be at least equivalent to what Australian employees in the same role earn (the employer cannot pay a sponsored worker less than Australian comparators). Underpayment of a sponsored worker relative to Australian comparators is both a nomination condition violation and a Fair Work Act breach.
non_obvious_action_required: Draft detailed, genuine job advertisements and publish on at least two approved channels. Retain timestamped screenshots of ads, application logs, and records of all Australian candidates assessed — these must be produced during a DHA compliance audit. Prepare a market salary rate analysis for the nominated occupation. Confirm that guaranteed annual earnings calculation uses base salary only — bonus, commission, and overtime are excluded from TSMIT assessment.

step: Skills Assessment (Occupation-Dependent — ACS, Engineers Australia, VETASSESS, etc.)
authority: Relevant Assessing Authority (ACS for ICT; Engineers Australia for engineers; VETASSESS for many professional/trade; CPA Australia or CAANZ for accountants)
deadline_label: Before visa application can be finalised — allow 6–16 weeks depending on assessing body
non_obvious_official_guidance: Certain 482 and 186 occupations require a positive skills assessment from a designated assessing authority before the visa can be granted. The assessing body is occupation-specific: ACS for ICT professionals, Engineers Australia for engineers, VETASSESS for a broad range of professional and technical occupations, and CPA Australia or CAANZ for accountants, among others.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Skills assessments are the most commonly overlooked pre-departure step by employers. Two non-obvious traps: (1) Many employers assume skills assessments are only required for permanent visas — in fact, a subset of 482 occupations also require mandatory assessments, and DHA will not grant the visa without a positive outcome. (2) The ACS assessment for ICT professionals evaluates whether the candidate's qualifications and experience genuinely align with the nominated ANZSCO code, not just whether the candidate is technically competent. A software developer with a non-ICT degree nominated under ANZSCO 261313 may receive a negative assessment even with 10 years' experience, requiring a skills-based pathway assessment that adds 8+ weeks. Assessment fees range from AUD 500 to AUD 1,200+ and are typically borne by the employee, creating a potential negotiation point in relocation packages.
non_obvious_action_required: At pathway assessment stage, confirm for the specific ANZSCO code and visa subclass whether a skills assessment is mandatory. Do not wait for SBS approval or nomination lodgement to initiate — begin the assessment immediately after offer acceptance. Provide the candidate with the relevant assessing body's requirements checklist; most require certified copies of academic transcripts, a prescribed-format CV, and detailed employer reference letters.

step: Visa Application — Subclass 482 TSS or 186 ENS (Individual)
form_name: Online via ImmiAccount (medical examination via HAP ID assigned in ImmiAccount)
deadline_label: After nomination lodgement — concurrent processing available; allow 6–16 weeks for processing

step: Health Examination — DHA Panel Physician
authority: Department of Home Affairs — Approved Panel Physician
form_name: HAP ID (assigned via ImmiAccount; no paper form)
deadline_label: When HAP ID is assigned during processing — book immediately, do not wait for DHA prompt
non_obvious_official_guidance: Most 482 and 186 applicants must undergo a health examination by a DHA-approved panel physician. The examination includes a chest X-ray (tuberculosis screen) and medical history review. Results are submitted electronically by the physician directly to DHA.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Two non-obvious traps: (1) Panel physician appointment availability is highly variable by city — Sydney and Melbourne typically have 1–2 week waits; Perth and Brisbane can be 3–5 weeks; regional areas may require inter-city travel to the nearest approved physician. Waiting for DHA to prompt before booking can add 3–4 weeks to the overall timeline. (2) Health examinations have a 12-month validity window — if the visa is not granted within 12 months of the examination date (rare for 482 but possible for 186 ENS given processing times), a repeat examination is required at the applicant's cost (typically AUD 350–550 per adult). Dependants on the same visa application must complete separate examinations.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the health examination on the same day the HAP ID is assigned in ImmiAccount. Locate the nearest approved panel physician at homeaffairs.gov.au before departure if the employee is in a regional or international location. Briefing dependants on the requirement before they depart the origin country.

step: Police Clearance Certificates (All Countries of Residence — Past 10 Years)
authority: Police authority in each country of 12-month+ residence in the past 10 years
deadline_label: Obtain before or concurrent with visa application — validity periods vary by issuing country

step: Visa Entitlement Verification Online (VEVO) — Right-to-Work Check
deadline_label: Before the first day of work — employer statutory obligation under the Migration Act 1958
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers have a statutory obligation under the Migration Act 1958 to verify that each foreign national holds a valid visa with unrestricted work rights before employment commences. The VEVO system (business.gov.au/vevo) allows employers to check visa grant date, conditions, and work entitlements in real time. Employing an unlawful non-citizen or a visa holder whose conditions prohibit (or limit) work attracts civil penalties of up to AUD 345,000 per worker for a body corporate.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The most common VEVO trap is overlooking work limitation conditions that are invisible at surface level. Student visa holders (subclass 500) are limited to 48 hours per fortnight during study periods. Working Holiday Maker visa holders (417/462) have an employer tenure restriction — working more than 6 months with one employer is prohibited without a specific exemption. Graduate visa holders (485) have no hour limits but must be residing in Australia. The other major trap is treating a visa grant notification email as a physical document — Australia does not issue paper visas or stamp passports; the grant email plus a VEVO check is the legally correct evidence of grant. HR teams that file only the email and never run VEVO have no defence against a compliance audit. Visa conditions must also be rechecked whenever an employee's role or hours change.
non_obvious_action_required: Run a VEVO check for every foreign national before Day 1 of employment. Set a calendar reminder to recheck 90 days before visa expiry and whenever the employee's role changes. Retain records of each VEVO check for at least 2 years. For 482 visa holders, confirm that Condition 8107 (must work only in the nominated occupation for the approved sponsor) is not breached by any planned title changes, secondments, or role expansions.

step: Tax File Number (TFN) Application — Australian Taxation Office
form_name: Online TFN application via myGov (residents) or NAT 1432 paper form (non-residents); also available at Australia Post for eligible migrants
deadline_label: Apply on Day 1 or 2 of arrival — TFN arrives by post within 2–28 days
non_obvious_official_guidance: A Tax File Number (TFN) is a unique identifier issued by the ATO used across tax, superannuation, and government benefit systems. All employees working in Australia must quote their TFN to their employer. New migrants holding a visa that authorises work can apply online via myGov, at an Australia Post outlet, or via the ATO website.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Without a TFN on file, the employer is legally required to withhold PAYG tax at the top marginal rate (47%) plus the Medicare levy on all wages — this is 'no-TFN withholding' and causes significant over-withholding for the first 1–4 payroll cycles. Three traps: (1) Processing time is variable and unpredictable — online applications for migrants can take 4–28 days depending on ATO workload; the TFN is mailed to the Australian residential address (not emailed or available via the ATO portal). A wrong address at application time means the letter is undeliverable and a new application is required. (2) An application reference number is not a TFN substitute — the ATO does not formally accept reference numbers for withholding reduction purposes, though some payroll systems accept them informally. (3) TFNs from prior Australian work periods (e.g., a student visa stint 5 years earlier) remain valid — employees should check myGov for an existing TFN before applying, to avoid duplicate records.
non_obvious_action_required: Brief the employee to apply for a TFN on Day 1 or 2 using the visa grant number and confirmed Australian residential address. Alert payroll that the first 1–4 pay cycles may require maximum withholding. Confirm the residential address in advance — TFN letters cannot be redirected. If an existing TFN exists from a prior visit, retrieve it via myGov rather than applying again.

step: Medicare Enrolment (+ Reciprocal Health Care Agreement Eligibility Check)
form_name: MS004 — Medicare enrolment form (completed in person at a Services Australia service centre)
deadline_label: Within first 2 weeks of arrival — in person at a Services Australia centre; interim certificate available on the day
non_obvious_official_guidance: Medicare provides access to subsidised healthcare in Australia. Eligible groups include: Australian citizens, permanent residents, New Zealand citizens, and temporary visa holders from Reciprocal Health Care Agreement (RHCA) countries where their specific visa type is covered. RHCA countries: United Kingdom, Ireland, New Zealand, Sweden, Netherlands, Belgium, Norway, Slovenia, Malta, Italy, and Finland.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Four non-obvious traps: (1) RHCA coverage is not comprehensive healthcare — it covers 'immediately necessary' and 'urgent' medical treatment only. It does not cover elective procedures, dental, optical, physiotherapy, or ambulance in most states. It also does not cover gap payments above the Medicare Benefits Schedule rate. Employees from RHCA countries who assume Medicare equals comprehensive healthcare end up with significant out-of-pocket costs and dissatisfaction. (2) Most 482 visa holders from non-RHCA countries — India, China, the Philippines, Brazil, South Africa, the US, Canada, and the majority of the world — are not eligible for Medicare at all. Private health insurance is not optional for these employees; it is a genuine relocation cost the employer must factor into the package. (3) The Medicare levy (2% of taxable income) is withheld via PAYG from all employees without exemption by default — Medicare-ineligible employees can apply for a Medicare Levy Exemption Certificate (NAT 0929) to remove this withholding. Without the certificate, they pay a levy for a system they cannot access. (4) Medicare cards take 2–4 weeks to arrive by post; the Services Australia centre issues a printed interim certificate on the day of enrolment, which is accepted by most GP clinics.
non_obvious_action_required: At the pathway assessment stage, check the employee's country of citizenship against the RHCA list. For non-RHCA employees: arrange private health insurance before departure and include the cost explicitly in the relocation package budget. For RHCA-eligible employees: enrol at a Services Australia centre on arrival with passport, visa grant evidence, and Australian residential address. Apply for a Medicare Levy Exemption Certificate (NAT 0929) for all non-eligible employees before the first payroll.

step: Australian Bank Account Opening
deadline_label: Within first week of arrival — required for salary payment and super contributions

step: Superannuation Fund Selection — Standard Choice Form (NAT 13080) and Stapled Fund Check
authority: Australian Taxation Office (ATO) / Superannuation fund trustees
deadline_label: Employer must offer choice within 28 days of commencement; issue the form on Day 1
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must offer eligible employees a choice of superannuation fund using the ATO Standard Choice Form (NAT 13080) within 28 days of employment commencement. If the employee does not return a completed form, the employer must check whether the employee has a 'stapled super fund' by querying the ATO via Online Services for Business, and contribute to that fund. If no stapled fund exists, the employer defaults to its nominated MySuper product.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The stapled fund rule (introduced 1 November 2021) is the most systematically overlooked superannuation compliance obligation. Before the rule, employers simply defaulted all new employees to their MySuper fund — that is now a legal violation if the employee has a stapled fund. The employer must actively query the ATO stapled fund system using the employee's TFN (another reason TFN collection is urgent — no TFN, no stapled fund query). For new migrants who have never previously worked in Australia there will be no stapled fund and defaulting to MySuper is correct. Three additional traps: (1) The SG rate is 11.5% of ordinary time earnings (OTE) for 2024-25, rising to 12% from 1 July 2025 — the rate is legislated to increase annually and payroll systems must be updated each 1 July without exception. (2) SG is calculated on OTE (base salary, commissions, ordinary allowances) — not on overtime, expense reimbursements, or bonuses paid for non-ordinary hours. Miscategorising OTE leads to either SG shortfalls or over-payment. (3) SG contributions must be received by the fund by the quarterly due date — a payment that leaves the employer's bank account on time but is received by the fund one day late due to banking processing still triggers the Superannuation Guarantee Charge, which is non-deductible for the employer.
non_obvious_action_required: Issue the Standard Choice Form on Day 1. If no form is returned within 28 days: run a stapled super fund request via ATO Online Services for Business using the employee's TFN. Set a 1 July annual reminder to confirm the SG rate update in all payroll systems. For employees on total remuneration packages, review employment contracts to determine whether the SG rate increase on 1 July 2025 (to 12%) is absorbed or adds to total package cost. Brief new migrants on the Departing Australia Superannuation Payment (DASP) process for when they eventually leave Australia permanently.

step: TFN Notification to Employer — Tax File Number Declaration (NAT 3092)
deadline_label: As soon as TFN is received — typically 2–28 days after application; follow up ATO at 13 28 61 if not received by Day 28

step: Tax Residency Declaration and PAYG Withholding Category
form_name: Tax File Number Declaration (NAT 3092) — residency question on this form
deadline_label: On commencement — first payroll cannot be processed correctly without this declaration
non_obvious_official_guidance: The ATO's tax residency determination governs whether an employee is taxed as an Australian resident (progressive rates starting at 0% for income up to AUD 18,200, plus low income tax offset) or a foreign resident (flat 32.5% from the first dollar, no tax-free threshold, no LITO). The primary test is the 'resides' test (ordinary concepts of actual residence); secondary tests are the domicile test and 183-day test.
non_obvious_actual_reality: This is the highest-stakes payroll classification in an international employee move. Two critical traps: (1) A new migrant who intends to live and work in Australia long-term is typically an Australian tax resident from Day 1 of arrival under the resides test — not after 183 days. The 183-day rule is a secondary fallback test. Payroll systems that default all new overseas hires to 'foreign resident' withholding for the first 6 months systematically over-withhold at 32.5% when the employee should be taxed at resident progressive rates. The employee then reconciles via their tax return, but this creates a significant cash-flow disadvantage and employee relations friction. Conversely, a 482 holder on a 2-year Short-term stream is not automatically a non-resident — a short visa duration does not determine tax residency. (2) The correct classification for genuinely ambiguous cases (e.g., an assignment of 12–18 months with an unclear intention to remain) requires reference to ATO Tax Ruling TR 2023/1, which updated the residency analysis following the Full Federal Court decision in Harding v Commissioner of Taxation. Employers who classify incorrectly face PAYG withholding shortfall liability.
non_obvious_action_required: At commencement, have the employee complete NAT 3092 and self-assess their residency status with employer guidance. Brief employees that they are self-assessing; recommend a registered tax agent for genuinely uncertain cases. Do not apply a blanket 'foreign resident for first 6 months' policy — it is legally incorrect and creates reconciliation complexity. Flag employees on short-term assignments (under 2 years) for a 183-day residency review.

step: Medicare Levy Exemption Certificate — Non-RHCA Employees (NAT 0929)
form_name: Application for a Medicare Levy Exemption Certificate (NAT 0929)
deadline_label: Apply before first payroll — certificate issued within 2–4 weeks of ATO application
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employees who are not entitled to Medicare benefits — principally temporary visa holders from non-RHCA countries — can apply for a Medicare Levy Exemption Certificate to prevent the employer withholding the Medicare levy (2% of taxable income) from wages. The ATO issues a certificate covering a specified period; the employer applies the exemption code in the payroll system.
non_obvious_actual_reality: If the exemption certificate is not obtained before the first payroll, the 2% Medicare levy is withheld from Day 1 and the employee must reclaim it via their individual tax return at financial year-end — a delay of up to 12 months. For an employee earning AUD 120,000, this is AUD 2,400 in interest-free over-withholding. Employers who do not manage this systematically create a recurring grievance with relocated staff, who correctly feel they are lending money to the ATO for a service they cannot access. The certificate covers all temporary visa holders who are not from RHCA countries — which includes most 482 holders from the US, India, China, Brazil, South Africa, Japan, South Korea, and the majority of the world. The certificate must be renewed annually.
non_obvious_action_required: At the RHCA eligibility check (arrival week), classify each new employee as Medicare-eligible or ineligible. For ineligible employees: apply to the ATO for a NAT 0929 certificate before the first payroll is processed. Brief payroll to hold the Medicare levy withholding in a suspense account pending certificate receipt and then apply the exemption retroactively to any payrolls processed without the certificate. Set an annual calendar reminder for certificate renewal.

step: PAYG Withholding Registration — ATO (Linked to ABN)
form_name: PAYG withholding registration via ABN registration (ATO Business Portal or ATO Online Services)
deadline_label: Before first wages payment — registration required to withhold and remit legally

step: State Payroll Tax Registration (State-Specific Thresholds Apply)
authority: State Revenue Office in each jurisdiction (e.g., Revenue NSW; SRO Victoria; Queensland Revenue Office; RevenueSA; State Revenue WA; ACT Revenue Office; Territory Revenue Office NT)
form_name: Online registration via relevant state revenue office portal
deadline_label: Within 7 days of exceeding the state monthly threshold in any month — do not wait for end-of-year
non_obvious_official_guidance: Each Australian state and territory levies payroll tax on employers whose total Australian wages exceed the jurisdiction's annual threshold. 2024-25 rates and thresholds (approximate — verify with each SRO): NSW 5.45% (AUD 1.2M threshold); VIC 4.85% (AUD 900,000); QLD 4.75%–4.95% (AUD 1.3M); SA 4.95% (AUD 1.5M); WA 5.5% (AUD 1M); ACT 6.85% (AUD 2M); NT 5.5% (AUD 1.5M). Wages include salary, superannuation contributions, fringe benefits, and certain contractor payments.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Two major traps for employers establishing an Australian presence: (1) Grouping provisions — if the new Australian entity is related to overseas entities or has common ownership with any other Australian entity, all related group members' Australian wages are aggregated to assess whether any state's threshold is exceeded. A multinational corporation with an existing Australian subsidiary cannot treat its new subsidiary's wages as a standalone calculation. In practice, many new-entity payrolls cross a state threshold on the first hire because the group total was already at or above the threshold. (2) Remote-work multi-state obligations — payroll tax is levied by the state where the work is performed, not where the employer is registered. An employer headquartered in NSW with a sponsored employee working from home in Victoria must register with the Victorian SRO if Victorian wages exceed Victoria's threshold. With post-COVID normalisation of remote work, multi-state payroll tax exposure has become routine for any employer with more than one work location.
non_obvious_action_required: Map all states where employees will perform work before the first hire is made. Confirm whether any related-entity grouping applies by reviewing shareholding and common control. Register in each applicable state before wages are paid. For the first international hire into a newly established Australian entity in a multinational group, brief the finance and group tax teams on the grouping threshold assessment. Review annually as wage levels change.

step: Fair Work Information Statement and Casual Employment Information Statement (if applicable)
form_name: Fair Work Information Statement (published by the Fair Work Ombudsman; Casual Employment Information Statement for casual employees)
deadline_label: Before or as soon as practicable after commencement — a condition of the National Employment Standards

step: Visa Condition 8107 Compliance — Nominated Occupation and Approved Sponsor
deadline_label: Ongoing — assess at every role change, title change, promotion, secondment, or restructure affecting a 482 visa holder
non_obvious_official_guidance: Subclass 482 visa holders are granted with Condition 8107, which requires the visa holder to work only in the nominated occupation for the approved sponsor. The nominated occupation corresponds to the ANZSCO code in the approved nomination. Working in a materially different occupation — regardless of employer consent or salary — is a breach of visa conditions subject to visa cancellation.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Condition 8107 is the most systematically breached condition in employer-sponsored visa programs in Australia. Two dominant scenarios: (1) Promotions and title changes — a software engineer (ANZSCO 261313) promoted to Engineering Manager after 18 months has materially different duties and the new role is not covered by the original ANZSCO code; a new nomination must be lodged and approved before the role change takes effect. Employers who simply update the internal job title without a new nomination expose the employee to visa cancellation risk. DHA compliance inspections routinely identify these breaches through comparison of payslip job titles against approved nomination records. (2) Secondments and client-site work — if a 482 visa holder is assigned to work for or at a related entity, a client, or a joint venture partner even temporarily, that secondary entity must itself be an approved work sponsor; the employee cannot work for any entity other than their approved sponsor. Emergency client-site deployments that circumvent this rule are a common trap in professional services and IT consulting.
non_obvious_action_required: Build an HR workflow that triggers automatic 8107 review for any employment change affecting a 482 visa holder: role change, title change, restructure, secondment, or client-site deployment. Lodge a new nomination before (not after) the change takes effect — acting retrospectively is legally ineffective. Document all 8107 compliance assessments and who made the determination. If an inadvertent breach is identified, seek immigration legal advice immediately — voluntary disclosure to DHA is generally preferable to discovery during an audit.

step: Superannuation Guarantee Rate Annual Update (1 July)
field_label: SG Rate Update in Payroll System
deadline_label: Effective 1 July each year — payroll system must apply the new rate from the first payroll of the new financial year
non_obvious_official_guidance: The Superannuation Guarantee rate is legislated to increase annually: 11.5% (2024-25) and 12% (2025-26 onward). Employers must apply the correct rate to all SG contributions from 1 July each year.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Payroll systems that are not manually updated on 1 July will calculate the prior year's SG rate for the first payroll of the new financial year, creating an SG shortfall that must be corrected via the SGC process (non-deductible, interest-bearing). The risk is highest for employers using legacy payroll software or manual calculations. For employees on total remuneration packages that bundle base salary and super, the annual rate increase raises the employer's cost from 1 July unless the contract specifies the package is inclusive of super at whatever rate applies — a contract review question that is routinely skipped.
non_obvious_action_required: Add a recurring 1 July payroll task to verify the SG rate in all payroll systems. For 2025-26: ensure payroll reflects 12% from 1 July 2025. For total remuneration package employees, review employment contracts before 1 July to confirm whether the rate increase is absorbed into the package or adds to total cost, and communicate outcomes to affected employees.

step: Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 Reporting — Each Payroll Event
deadline_label: On or before each payroll payment date — real-time reporting obligation
non_obvious_official_guidance: Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 (mandatory from 1 March 2022) requires employers to report salary and wages, PAYG withholding, and superannuation information to the ATO on or before each payday via STP-enabled payroll software. Phase 2 expanded reporting to include disaggregated income types, employee tax treatment codes, working holiday maker status, and country of income tax residency.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The Phase 2 income type disaggregation and tax treatment code requirements are the non-obvious compliance trap for internationally mobile employees. Employers must report the correct income type code per employee (SAL for regular salary; WHM for working holiday makers; FEI for foreign employment income; others). An employee paid partly in Australia and partly offshore for the same period requires careful income allocation — payroll systems without international payroll capability often misclassify split-payroll arrangements. Tax treatment codes must also be set correctly from Day 1: incorrectly coding a tax resident as a foreign resident pre-fills the employee's ATO myTax return with wrong data, requiring an amendment that the employee must chase themselves. Non-lodgement attracts penalties of AUD 222 per 28-day period (Base Penalty Amount), with higher multiples for medium and large withholders.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm payroll software is STP Phase 2 certified. At onboarding, set the correct income type and tax treatment code for each new international hire — cross-reference with the residency determination and any dual-country payroll arrangement. Conduct an annual STP reconciliation before 14 July (the end-of-financial-year STP finalisation deadline) to identify and correct any reporting errors before they flow through to employee tax returns.

step: Departing Australia Superannuation Payment (DASP) — Employee Briefing and Departure Planning
form_name: DASP application via ATO online system (after visa ceases)
deadline_label: Applies after permanent departure from Australia once visa has ceased — no statutory deadline, but apply promptly to avoid fund consolidation complexity
non_obvious_official_guidance: Temporary visa holders (including 482 and 457 holders) who have permanently departed Australia may claim their accumulated superannuation as a Departing Australia Superannuation Payment (DASP) once their visa has ceased or been cancelled and they are not an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident. The DASP application is submitted online via the ATO.
non_obvious_actual_reality: DASP is systematically undercommunicated to departing employees and routinely generates the largest end-of-assignment surprise. Three non-obvious details: (1) DASP tax rates are punitive: for working holiday makers, 65% of the taxable component is withheld as tax; for other temporary visa holders (most 482 holders), 35% is withheld. An employee who accumulated AUD 50,000 in super over a 4-year assignment receives approximately AUD 32,500 after DASP tax. This is legally correct but uniformly experienced as a shock by departing employees who expected to receive their full balance. (2) The DASP application cannot be lodged while the employee still holds a valid Australian visa — the visa must first cease or be cancelled. This means the application is typically submitted from overseas, after departure. Applications with incomplete details (especially older super accounts without updated contact information) stall for months. (3) Super accounts from previous Australian work periods or prior employers may be held in different funds, including the ATO Unclaimed Super Money register if the account has been inactive. All accounts must be consolidated via myGov before the visa ceases — managing multiple funds from overseas is operationally difficult.
non_obvious_action_required: Brief all 482 visa holders on DASP at commencement (include a written summary in the relocation package) and again 3 months before anticipated departure. Advise consolidation of all super accounts via myGov before departure. Prepare an explicit statement of the DASP tax rate applicable to the employee's visa type — do not leave this as a discovery. If the employee has worked in Australia previously, have them check the ATO's Unclaimed Super register for any lost accounts.

step: Annual Individual Income Tax Return — Australian Financial Year
form_name: Individual tax return via myTax (myGov) or lodged by a registered tax agent
deadline_label: 31 October each year for self-lodgers; registered tax agent clients have extended deadlines (typically May of the following year)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Australian tax residents must lodge an individual income tax return for each financial year (1 July – 30 June) in which they earned taxable income. Non-residents with Australian-source income must also lodge. The return reconciles PAYG withholding, Medicare levy, and other obligations. The ATO pre-fills myTax returns with STP employer data, bank interest, dividend records, and private health insurance status.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Two non-obvious items for internationally mobile employees: (1) Year-of-arrival returns require pro-rating the tax-free threshold based on the number of months of Australian residency in the financial year. An employee who arrived in Australia on 1 March receives 4/12 of the full AUD 18,200 threshold (approximately AUD 6,067). The ATO's myTax system does not always calculate this correctly for partial-year residents; an incorrect return generates a notice of assessment that under or over-collects tax. Expat tax agents who specialise in part-year returns consistently cite this as the most common self-lodgement error. (2) Australian tax residents must declare worldwide income in their Australian return. An employee who earned salary in France in July (before arriving in Australia in October) must include the French income and claim a Foreign Income Tax Offset (FITO) for tax already paid in France. HR teams that do not brief relocated employees on worldwide income reporting expose them to ATO correction notices and potential penalties. Including a tax return preparation allowance for the first year in the relocation package is standard market practice.
non_obvious_action_required: Brief all relocated employees that the first-year return is complex and recommend a registered tax agent with expat experience. Confirm whether the relocation package includes a tax preparation allowance or tax equalisation arrangement for the first and departure years. Alert employees that the ATO myTax pre-fill for the year of arrival covers only the Australian portion and may not include foreign income. For employees who leave mid-year, brief them on the departure-year return obligations and the availability of non-resident tax treatment for the remainder of the year.

step: Visa Renewal or Permanent Residence Pathway — 186 ENS Temporary Residence Transition Stream
deadline_label: For 482 Medium-term holders: 186 TRT eligibility begins at 3 years on the 482; lodge well before 482 expiry — DHA 186 processing times range from 10 to 36 months
non_obvious_official_guidance: Subclass 482 Medium-term stream visa holders (MLTSSL occupations) become eligible for permanent residence via Subclass 186 ENS — Temporary Residence Transition (TRT) stream after at least 3 years of full-time work with the same sponsoring employer in the nominated occupation. Short-term stream 482 holders (STSOL occupations) are generally not eligible for the TRT stream and must either apply for a new 482, depart Australia, or apply via an alternative pathway.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Three non-obvious traps: (1) The 3-year clock starts from the 482 visa grant date, not the employment start date — and counts only periods of full-time (or equivalent) work. Extended unpaid leave (e.g., parental leave) does not automatically toll the clock, but DHA may scrutinise absences during a 186 TRT assessment and require statutory declarations confirming continuous employment. (2) The employer must lodge a fresh nomination for the 186 ENS — the existing 482 nomination does not convert automatically. The 186 nomination requires a new Deed of Agreement from the employer, updated evidence of SBS compliance and training benchmarks, and in some occupation categories a refreshed skills assessment. (3) Processing times for 186 applications have historically ranged from 10 to 36 months depending on DHA queue depth, occupation, and applicant country of birth. An employee whose 482 expires before the 186 is decided is placed on a Bridging Visa A (BVA) — they can continue working during this period but cannot travel internationally without a Bridging Visa B (BVB). Failing to lodge the 186 well in advance of the 482 expiry therefore creates travel restrictions that affect business travel.
non_obvious_action_required: Set a 2-year milestone review for all Medium-term stream 482 holders: confirm MLTSSL occupation still applies, confirm grant date (not commencement date) for 3-year eligibility, and begin preparing the 186 nomination package. Lodge the 186 before the 2.5-year mark of the 482 visa to allow for processing time before the visa expires. For Short-term stream 482 holders, initiate an alternative pathway assessment at 18 months — do not wait until the visa is near expiry.
